answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a refundable stake bond: each identity must lock tokens before trading, and the bond only unlocks after a slow cooldown, like cargo clearing a wharf. Spinning up a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand locked bonds, so an attacker pays linearly for every fake voice. If an identity cheats, peers can slash its bond, turning deception from cheap talk into a real loss. Honest agents keep a velvet-smooth reputation, while a falcon-eyed audit trail makes repeat offenders easy to spot and price out.
